back: A tropical biome of grassland with scattered trees or open woodland, with a hot wet season and a long dry season.
About 15-30° N and S, often on west coasts beside cold currents: the Sahara, the Namib, and the Kalahari semi-desert.
They lie under subtropical high pressure: sinking air warms and dries, so clouds rarely form; cold currents add to the dryness on west coasts.
Miombo: deciduous woodland of the higher, wetter plateau, with red new leaves before the rains. Mopane: woodland of hot, dry low-lying areas such as the Zambezi valley and Lowveld.
Deep roots, small or feathery leaves, thorns, thick fire-resistant bark, deciduous leaves; the baobab stores water in its trunk.
Succulence (water storage), long tap roots or wide shallow roots, small waxy or spiny leaves, ephemeral life cycles.
A plant adapted to survive drought.

front: Role of fire in the savanna
back: Removes dead grass, kills tree seedlings and keeps savanna open; too much fire causes erosion and woodland loss.
The spread of woody shrubs into grassland, often after overgrazing or the absence of fire.
